settings.sourceComposition: 4:3 historical visual grammar inside vertical-safe framing
settings.visualStyle: Grounded first-person WWII mountain infantry realism at Monte Cassino, May 1944. Polish II Corps soldier POV on steep rocky approaches, shattered masonry, terraced slopes, olive scrub, dust, smoke haze, broken cover and physically exhausting climbing. Terrain, fatigue, cover and limited visibility dominate the experience. German defenders are usually unseen or only briefly glimpsed at distance. Non-graphic combat only. No heroic posing, no cinematic glamour, no clean battlefield overview, no game HUD and no centered FPS weapon framing.
settings.customVisualStyle: Human-eye POV from a tired infantryman moving through real terrain. Short advances, pauses, crouching, crawling, waiting and recovering behind rocks or rubble. Natural head movement tied to body motion, breathing and balance. No gimbal glide, no floating camera, no cinematic reveals, no dramatic orbit shots, no perfect tracking and no impossible exposure on open slopes.
settings.customProjectStructure: 15 connected scenes x 8 seconds. Scene N end state must physically match Scene N+1 start state. The POV owner is never rendered as an external character. Nearby Polish soldiers move independently and do not perform for the viewer. German defenders remain physically separated in opposing terrain and are mostly inferred through rifle cracks, dust, ricochets, mortar impacts and brief movement behind cover.

rules: POV owner is never shown externally.
Normally no weapon is centered in frame.
Hands, rifle, sleeve or web gear appear only when naturally used.
Head movement follows body movement and balance rather than artificial handheld shake.
Standing, crouching and crawling heights must change naturally with terrain and danger.
The view may be blocked by rocks, rubble, squadmates, dust or smoke.
The POV can lose sight of action and should not always know where enemy fire originates.
No third-person shot, no floating camera, no gimbal glide, no cinematic orbit and no drone perspective.
povCameraLock.weaponVisibility: Weapon usually slung, lowered or only partly visible at frame edge. Shield-like FPS framing is forbidden.

monteCassinoRealityLock.movementPattern: short advance, stop, crouch, crawl, recover, then move again
rules: The mountain is a physical obstacle, not a scenic backdrop.
Loose stone, broken masonry and steep gradient slow movement.
The soldier rarely moves more than a few meters in exposed terrain without stopping.
Nearby troops use rocks, terrace walls, craters, rubble and ruined structures as cover.
Enemy fire is often heard or inferred before defenders are seen.
No clean heroic run up an open slope.
No large enemy group standing exposed for the camera.

movie.storyTitle: WWII Soldier POV EP08 — Monte Cassino: Up the Mountain
movie.storySummary: A fictional Polish II Corps infantryman climbs the devastated Monte Cassino approaches in May 1944. The episode focuses on the physical difficulty of the mountain: loose stone, broken terrace walls, rubble, limited cover, exhaustion and uncertain enemy fire. The soldier advances only in short movements, repeatedly crouches or drops behind cover, crosses one exposed gap, shelters in ruins, climbs toward a higher position and ends still under threat rather than in triumph.
movie.mainStoryPrompt: Create a two-minute grounded human-eye WWII soldier POV at Monte Cassino in May 1944. Make terrain, fatigue, cover and incomplete information more important than spectacle. The Polish II Corps POV soldier moves uphill through loose rock, broken terrace walls, rubble, ruined shelters and smoke haze. German defenders are usually not clearly visible; their presence is communicated through rifle cracks, ricochets, mortar bursts, dust and brief distant movement. The soldier advances only a few meters at a time, stops behind cover, crouches, crawls when necessary, breathes heavily and resumes movement only when possible. No heroic charge, no smooth climbing, no centered rifle, no cinematic reveal, no clean battlefield overview, no constant firing, no dialogue, no narration and no music.
